item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00404","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C06","C21"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both orders begin by delegating to the Secretary of State the President's functions, powers, and authority under a newly enacted international-assistance statute while reserving specified statutory provisions. Both then give the Secretary responsibility for directing or executing the statutory programs through cooperation with other federal departments, agencies, and wholly-owned government corporations. The close language and matching administrative structure are substantially more specific than generic delegation boilerplate. C06 has weaker parallels involving interagency consultation and advisory committees, while C21 contains only the simpler Secretary-of-State delegation
